permit.exempt_list_quote: 102.10 Work exempt from approval. Approval is not required for the following work; however, this work is still to comply with all applicable provisions of the rules of the board: Building: 1. One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed one hundred twenty square feet (11.15 m2) and playground structures. 2. Fences not over seven feet (1829 mm) high. 3. Retaining walls which are not over four feet (1219 mm) in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge or impounding Class I, II or III-A liquids. 4. Water tanks supported directly upon grade if the capacity does not exceed five thousand gallons (18 927 L) and the ratio of height to diameter or width does not exceed two to one. 5. Sidewalks, parking lots and driveways not more than thirty inches (762 mm) above grade and not over any basement or story below and which are not part of an accessible route. 6. Finishes not regulated by this code, decorating, or other work defined as maintenance or minor repair. 7. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. 8. Window awnings supported by an exterior wall of Group R-3. [items 9 to 18: temporary structures and tents, storage tanks, battery smoke alarms, crypts, signs, emergency occupancy] [...] 102.10.2 Minor repairs. Minor repairs to structures may be made without application or notice to the building official. Such repairs are not to include the cutting away of any wall, partition or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress, or rearrangement of parts of a structure affecting the egress requirements; nor do minor repairs include addition to, alteration of, replacement or relocation of any standpipe, water supply, sewer, drainage, drain leader, gas, soil, waste, vent or similar piping, electric wiring or mechanical or other work affecting public health or general safety.
permit.note: Columbus points to this state list: its FAQ says the complete list of work that needs no building permit is in Ohio Building Code 102.10. Toilet partitions or compartments are not named. Item 6 exempts 'finishes not regulated by this code', while the state pack shows the code does regulate toilet partitions as interior finish (HDPE fire test), so the list doesn't settle it. 'Partition' in 102.10.2 means a wall. The city's Approved Minor Work Permit List (Rev 3/2019) has no partition or restroom item. Columbus City Codes Title 41 (the city's own permit chapter) could not be opened.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Columbus job sites. Price your restroom, choose a material and see the Ohio rules Columbus enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Columbus offices, schools, university buildings and distribution centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Ohio's statewide building rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Columbus enforces them. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Columbus requires a permit, with plan review, for alterations to an existing building unless the work is exempt. The exempt list it uses is Ohio's, which covers decorating, maintenance, minor repairs and finishes the building rules don't regulate, and doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask Columbus Building and Zoning Services whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.install_rule: Columbus requires every contractor working in the city to hold the right city license or registration before applying for permits, and general contractors register with Columbus Building and Zoning Services. Ohio licenses only five commercial trades at state level: electrical, HVAC, hydronics, plumbing and refrigeration. Partition installation isn't one of them. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who applies for a permit in Columbus needs a city license or registration first.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on state, county and city projects over $250,000 for new construction or $75,000 for remodeling, Ohio law requires at least the wage the state sets for each trade in each county; school district projects are exempt from that law. The state publishes its Franklin County rates on a portal that needs a login. On federally funded building work in Franklin County, the federal rate for a carpenter is $35.94 an hour plus $23.59 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8% in Columbus: 5.75% state, 1.25% Franklin County and 1% transit authority.
page.buyers_extra: - **Colleges and university buildings:** HDPE or phenolic for heavy daily use, with extra-privacy stalls in residence halls and student centers.
